page: The UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-8GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Starter family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 40 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring 3854.38 in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and achieving high throughput in single-threaded compression tasks, such as 41.31 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.43 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15535.47 and a Passmark CPU score of 13141.51. Memory performance represents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 850.79 GB/sec, the overall Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25% tier.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that require strong single-threaded burst capabilities but do not demand sustained, dedicated multi-core execution. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and small-scale text processing or utility scripts. The inclusion of local SSD storage and a public IPv4 address enhances its utility for development and testing environments without requiring additional resource provisioning.
